IKEv1.message: IKEv1 is deprecated (RFC 8247) and vulnerable to offline dictionary attacks.

DES.message: DES provides zero confidentiality against modern attacks.

3DES.message: 3DES is a legacy 64-bit block cipher vulnerable to SWEET32 (CVE-2016-2183).

AES-CBC-128.message: AES-CBC is phasing out. Vulnerable to padding oracles if MAC is misconfigured.

AES-CBC-256.message: AES-CBC is phasing out. Vulnerable to padding oracles if MAC is misconfigured.

MD5.message: MD5 is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to collisions.

SHA1.message: SHA1 is deprecated due to theoretical collision weaknesses.

14.message: Group 14 (MODP2048) meets baseline 112-bit security, but ECC transition recommended.

MONOTONIC.message: ESP sequence numbers are present and monotonically incrementing per-SPI (RFC 4303 §3.3.3 sender compliance verified). Note: receiver-side anti-replay window enforcement is local policy and not observable from passive capture.

DUPLICATE_SEQ.message: Duplicate ESP sequence numbers detected within the same SPI — the sender is violating RFC 4303 §3.3.3 (MUST NOT generate duplicate sequence numbers). This undermines anti-replay protection even if the receiver's window is correctly configured.

NON_MONOTONIC.message: ESP sequence numbers are not strictly monotonically incrementing per-SPI. This may indicate packet reordering or a non-conformant implementation. Anti-replay window may still function if gaps are within window size, but sender compliance cannot be confirmed.
